correctness.rationale: The connected-graph two-step Laplacian kernel forces the consecutive firing indicator vectors of a primitive period-two state to be complementary, and local threshold inequalities yield exactly o_v(f) independently selectable chip values per vertex; dividing oriented phases by two gives N(G)=sum_f prod_v o_v(f)/2. For K_{n,n}, grouping left/right firing counts (i,j) produces q_n(i,j)=Pr[Bin(n,1-j/n)=i]Pr[Bin(n,1-i/n)=j]; the local Gaussian along i+j=n yields sum q_n~sqrt(pi*n)/2 and the normalized Beta(1/2,1/2) marginal; maximal binomial-mass bounds make both tails negligible. For deletion H_n with max degree R fixed, each removed edge has exactly 2/n conditional expected logarithmic cut-weight contribution; bounded-degree fixed-size sampling gives O_R(1/n) variance on each interior strip, hence uniform E[exp(-X)]~exp(-2|E(H_n)|/n). Endpoint domination extends uniformity and log degree product=-2m_n/n+O_R(1/n). Thus N(G_n)/N(K_{n,n})=exp(-2m_n/n)(1+o_R(1)) and N(G_n)~sqrt(pi*n)/4 prod_v degree_G(v) uniformly; the arcsine phase law survives. This proves only primitive period-two configurations, not attraction basins or all possible periods.

value.rationale: This is a natural robustness theorem for exactly solvable parallel chip firing: arbitrary adversarial bounded-degree edge deletions destroy exchangeability, yet the asymptotic orbit census retains a universal edge-number factor and the nonuniform arcsine marginal. It determines asymptotic behavior for infinitely many irregular graph families, not just one small example or a renamed exact counting identity.
